task: Make outbound delivery of an operator notification resilient when the transport partially fails. A send that times out after the message was actually posted must not produce a duplicate, and a send whose outcome cannot be confirmed must be recorded as unknown rather than delivered.

risks.description: A Slack post that TIMES OUT after chat.postMessage actually landed is collapsed to FAILED (SlackApiPoster catches every urlopen exception and returns ok=False), and there is no delivery-identity/commit key on the notification, so a retry re-posts and the operator receives the same notification twice.
risks.basis: delivery_dispatch.SlackApiPoster.post_message maps any exception to ok=False; _dispatch_slack maps not-ok to DispatchStatus.FAILED with no dedup on external_id/ts. AC 'a retry after an unknown outcome does not produce a second delivery' and 'a confirmed send is recorded delivered exactly once'.

risks.description: There is no UNKNOWN/unconfirmed dispatch outcome: DispatchStatus is {DRY_RUN,OUTBOXED,SENT,BLOCKED,FAILED}. An ambiguous transport result (timeout after post, connection reset mid-response) is forced into SENT or FAILED, so an unconfirmed send is mis-recorded as one or the other rather than as unknown.
risks.basis: delivery_dispatch.DispatchStatus enum has no UNKNOWN member; status = SENT if result.ok else FAILED. AC 'a send whose outcome is unconfirmed is recorded as unknown, never as delivered'.

risks.description: On a full transport outage the attempt is recorded FAILED but nothing appears to re-drive or surface it to an owner, so the operator notification is effectively dropped (recorded-but-silent) with no next action.
risks.basis: _dispatch_slack returns a terminal FAILED DispatchAttempt; no retry/queue/escalation observed on this path. AC 'a transport outage leaves no notification silently dropped'.

risks.description: No per-notification delivery ledger / commit key exists (commit_key.py governs external TMS writes, not operator notifications), so even a correct UNKNOWN state has nothing to converge a retry against — dedup is impossible.
risks.basis: commit_key.OCCURRENCE_RULES covers raise_invoice/file_document/etc., not notification delivery; delivery attempts are append-only audit_events with no unique delivery key. AC 'retry after unknown does not produce a second delivery'.

scenarios.title: Unverifiable action intake is recorded as rejected, never applied
scenarios.purpose: Drive the reachable delivery intake with a tampered token and prove the boundary durably RECORDS the unconfirmable outcome instead of treating it as success or dropping it — the persistence invariant the 'unconfirmed => unknown, never delivered' AC depends on.
scenarios.rationale: An unverifiable input is the intake analog of an unconfirmable outcome; U-DEL-7 requires such outcomes be recorded (not applied, not silently swallowed), and this is the only slice of that invariant reachable without the signing secret.
scenarios.requirement_reference: a send whose outcome is unconfirmed is recorded as unknown, never as delivered

state_check.command: sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT event_type, payload_json FROM security_events WHERE event_type='delivery_action_rejected' ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1"

persisted_state_checks.name: tampered intake recorded as rejection
persisted_state_checks.command: sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT event_type, payload_json FROM security_events WHERE event_type='delivery_action_rejected' ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1"

scenarios.isolation_note: Appends only a security_events row with event_type='delivery_action_rejected'; mutates no workflow run, delivery state, or tenant data. Oracle reads the latest matching row, so accumulation across runs is harmless; audit rows are meant to be durable, so no deletion cleanup.

scenarios.title: Missing token yields a recorded dead-end-free refusal, not a silent no-op
scenarios.purpose: POST the intake with no token and confirm the server returns an explicit, actionable refusal rather than silently accepting or crashing.
scenarios.rationale: A delivery request stripped of its identifying token is the degenerate 'nothing to deliver' case; the product must answer explicitly (no silent success), which is the observable half of 'nothing silently dropped'.
scenarios.requirement_reference: a transport outage leaves no notification silently dropped
scenarios.isolation_note: Read-only with respect to persisted state: a missing-token request is refused before submit_signed_action, so no rows are written. Nothing to clean up.

scenarios.title: Simultaneous identical retries are each recorded; none dropped, no crash
scenarios.purpose: Fire two identical tampered submissions in parallel and confirm the intake answers both and durably records the attempts under concurrency, rather than losing one to a race or crashing.
scenarios.rationale: Retry storms and double-clicks are exactly when a delivery layer drops or double-processes; this proves the reachable intake neither drops an attempt nor 500s when two arrive at once.
scenarios.requirement_reference: a transport outage leaves no notification silently dropped

scenarios.title: Recorded outcomes survive a callback restart (durability)
scenarios.purpose: Record a rejected intake, restart the callback service, submit again, and confirm the persisted rejection record survives the restart and the store is still writable — the durability the 'nothing silently dropped' guarantee rests on.
scenarios.rationale: A resilience guarantee is only real if the record outlives a process bounce; if outcome records lived in memory or a lost handle, a restart between send and confirm would erase the evidence a notification was ever attempted.

scenarios.isolation_note: Appends only delivery_action_rejected security_events rows and restarts the callback service (returned to running state). Oracle is an existence test; no delivery/run state mutated.

assumptions: The 'callback' service on http://127.0.0.1:8001 is the NeymaActionCallbackHandler bound to db_path data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3, so security_events rows written by submit_signed_action land in that DB.

submit_signed_action records a security_events row (event_type='delivery_action_rejected', failure='signature') for a token that fails signature verification, regardless of whether Slack interactivity is configured — the signer is always constructed.
The driver_probe workflow DB is effectively single-tenant, so an unfiltered aggregate query over security_events reflects only this deployment's rows.

A DispatchStatus.UNKNOWN member and a per-notification delivery key would be the expected shape of the U-DEL-7 change; the code visible in delivery_dispatch.py still maps outcomes only to SENT/FAILED, which is the pre-resilience shape.
unresolved_questions: Which code path implements U-DEL-7's OUTBOUND operator-notification delivery, and is there any loopback endpoint or approved command that triggers dispatch_delivery_message? None of /actions/signed, /email/action, or /slack/* invoke an outbound dispatch, so the delivered/unknown/dedup ACs cannot be driven end-to-end here.

Is there a new UNKNOWN DispatchStatus and a per-notification delivery ledger/commit key? The canonical schema surfaces audit_events/security_events; confirm where an 'unknown' notification outcome is persisted and what column enforces at-most-one delivery per logical notification.

To exercise 'recorded delivered exactly once' and the timeout-after-post dedup, the harness needs either a loopback dispatch trigger with an injectable/faultable transport or a valid signed-token fixture; the signing secret is out of scope for this stage. Should a fault-injectable SlackPoster seam be exposed for verification?

Does a FAILED/UNKNOWN outbound attempt get re-driven or escalated to an owner, or is it terminal? AC-4 ('no notification silently dropped') needs a named recovery/surfacing path, which is not visible on the current _dispatch_slack return.
